subject: Re: Follow-up: caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@aptivion.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens

Hi Jamie — great meeting earlier. Quick recap and the numbers we discussed so both sides are aligned before Marcus and I draft a pilot scope.

Summary of your ask / target
- Monthly token run-rate: initially 300M-1.2B tokens (spikes during promo windows).
- Target effective unit economics: roughly $600-$800 per 1M tokens (budget constraint: ~$720/1M preferred).
- Primary traffic: conversational assistants with long reused prefixes (system prompts + customer context).

Redwood caching assumptions we discussed
- Base (list) inference cost used for modeling: $1,200 per 1M tokens (this is our hosted list benchmark for the selected model family).
- Prefix cache expected hit-rate: central estimate 35% (range: 20% conservative - 50% optimistic). This is for a prefix-caching strategy keyed off conversation_id + normalized system prompt, TTL 24h and 30-day retention for high-value prefixes.
- Effective pricing calculation (simple model where cache hits avoid model execution):
  - Conservatively (20% hits): $1,200 * (1 - 0.20) = $960 per 1M tokens effective
  - Central (35% hits): $1,200 * (1 - 0.35) = $780 per 1M tokens effective
  - Optimistic (50% hits): $1,200 * (1 - 0.50) = $600 per 1M tokens effective

Notes/assumptions: caching here refers to prefix/KV cache reuse (not just client-side tokens). Hit rate depends heavily on how standard your system prompts and customer context are across sessions and on session churn. We also assume cached responses are acceptable for your compliance and freshness constraints; some flows will be marked non-cacheable (billing/PII-sensitive prompts).

Attachments: I attached a short workbook (Redwood_Caching_Assumptions.xlsx) that replicates the above calcs and lets us swap in your real list price expectations and retention windows. Also attaching a draft mutual action plan.

Proposed next steps
1) Aptivion: share a week of anonymized prompt/response metadata (session_id, prefix_hash, tokens_in_request, cacheable_flag) — just metadata; no PII.
2) Redwood: run a 7-day sandbox run to measure empirical prefix hit rates and produce an effective $/1M tokens projection.
3) If the pilot confirms ~35%+ hit rate, we draft a pricing commitment that targets the $700-$800 effective range with an annual commit to get Preferred pricing.

Can you confirm the token ranges above (300M-1.2B) and whether you can share the metadata slice (step 1) next week?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

P.S. If helpful I can have Marcus send a short note on how we instrument hit rates and what the data payloads look like.

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly the kind of clarity we need. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Volume: the 300M-1.2B is accurate; Q1 ramp expected to be toward the lower end, Q3 promo could push toward the top of that range.
- Budget: our finance guardrail is $700/1M tokens effective; procurement will stretch to $800/1M if the pilot shows clear hit rates and SLA targets.
- Cache constraints: customer-configured system prompts are pretty standardized across ~60% of sessions. We can flag sensitive flows via a cacheable_flag.

We can extract the week of anonymized metadata you requested. Procurement needs a short MSA + PO estimate before they approve the data share; I'll loop them in once Redwood sends a short attestation on data handling (metadata-only, no message bodies).

I confirm we can provide the metadata slice by 2026-11-08 if Redwood provides the template.

Jamie
VP Product, Aptivion
jamie@aptivion.ai

On the PO side: procurement@aptivion.ai will need an initial cost estimate / pilot cost and a sample SOW.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: caching assumptions & effective $/1M tokens

Looping in a quick technical note for the SOW/attestation for procurement and a proposed pilot scope.

Technical fidelity
- What we need from Aptivion for hit-rate measurement: session_id (hashed), prefix_hash, is_cacheable boolean, timestamp, tokens_requested. No message bodies, no PII. We will sign an NDA/attestation for handling metadata only.
- Measurement approach: Redwood will run a dry-run in our sandbox that simulates cache keying and reports per-prefix hit counts and per-session effective token savings. We'll also instrument per-request latency impact.

Pilot SOW (7 days)
- Objective: measure prefix reuse and produce an observed hit-rate distribution across prefixes; compute effective $/1M tokens under 3 scenarios.
- Deliverables: hit-rate report, effective $/1M projection, recommended cache TTLs and percentile-based retention, a short note on any non-cacheable traffic.
- Estimated pilot cost: $3,000 (sandbox infra + engineering time). If Aptivion converts to a 12-month commit with expected annual volume > 3B tokens, the pilot cost will be credited to the first invoice.

Pricing sensitivity table (quick)
- List price: $1,200/1M tokens
- Effective price by hit rate: 20% -> $960; 35% -> $780; 50% -> $600.

Next operational steps I can own: draft the attestation and the short SOW. Marissa, can you send the SOW + attestation to Jamie and procurement by EOD? I’ll prepare the instrumentation checklist.

— Marcus
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
